description_full: CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings Inc. operates as a software as a service (SaaS) company for the property and casualty insurance economy in the United States and China. The company's cloud-based SaaS platform connects trading partners, facilitates commerce, and supports mission-critical, artificial intelligence enabled digital workflow across the insurers, repairers, automakers, parts suppliers, lenders, and others. It offers CCC insurance solutions, including CCC workflow, CCC estimating, CCC Total Loss, CCC subrogation, CCC automotive claim handling, CCC casualty, bodily injury claims synthesis, disability claims guidance, and workers' compensation claims guidance; CCC repair solutions, such as CCC estimating, CCC network management, CCC repair workflow, CCC repair quality, and CCC business-office solutions; CCC ecosystem and other solutions, which includes CCC parts solutions, CCC automotive manufacturer solutions, CCC diagnostics service provider solutions, and CCC payments; and CCC international solutions. CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings Inc. was founded in 1980 and is headquartered in Chicago, Illinois.

financial_summary: CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdi is a mid-cap technology business with a $4.5B market cap on $1.1B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +11% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +7.5pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 2% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 73% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $255M in free cash flow — roughly 24 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 186.90× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 7.6× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.3× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 13.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and stock-based comp at 17% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insiders hold 4.5% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
